content.comment_body: Hello [user_name], I'm new to automation and [company_name] products. I recently acquired a [product_name] for learning purposes. My issue is that [product_name] cannot upload the program to the device. After adjusting the IP as recommended and pinging the device successfully, the upload still fails. The software version I'm using is [version_no]. I tried both crossover and straight cables, used a USB Ethernet adapter, and tested several IP configurations, all with no success, despite the ping working. The program will not connect and seems to freeze. Any ideas on what could be wrong?
First, please share the IP address and subnet mask for your PC or laptop, as well as for the [product_name] device. Also, what error message appears? If possible, include a screenshot.

Hello [user_name], My computer and [product_name] device have matching IP settings: PC: 192.168.100.101 255.255.255.0 Gateway: blank [product_name]: 192.169.100.100 255.255.255.0 Gateway: 000.000.000.000 I also tried the default settings after a factory reset, adjusting my IP accordingly, but still no connection. The issue is worse now as the computer either freezes or becomes extremely slow.
That's not correct—the first three sections of the IP should be the same for both devices, with the last section different. Both should be 192.168.100.x.
Apologies, I made a mistake when entering the IPs here. On the actual computer and device, they're correct.
Are you seeing any error messages?

Hello, I've attached a PDF with several photos. Even after confirming settings, the computer freezes and only recovers with a hard reset. The software detects the device fine and shows status OK, but when attempting to connect, everything locks up.
No error message shows.

You mention trying to connect to a [product_name] at 192.168.2.134, but previously noted the address as 192.168.100.101. This mismatch could be an issue. Try the search function in [product_name] software, which will automatically detect available devices and display their IP and subnet mask.
In the attached network settings photo, I don't see the IP 192.168.100.101. Are there any error messages shown in the [product_name] software?

Current IP configuration: [product_name]: 192.168.2.134 255.255.255.0 Gateway: 0.0.0.0 PC: 192.168.2.135 255.255.255.0 Gateway: blank The software detects the device, MAC address matches, and ping replies correctly. However, attempting to connect causes the system to freeze. The IPs appear to be configured correctly.
Does anyone have [product_name] version [version_no] available for download? I want to test it but can't locate it.

Using [product_name] version [version_no] doesn't matter unless your device requires the newer version. If you have the latest hardware, ensure your software matches. Check if pressing the test button changes the line color from gray to green, indicating an active connection. Is the software installed and running with administrative rights?
No, pressing the test button does not turn it green—the software keeps trying to connect to the device but then freezes completely.
The photo displays the order number [article_no], which corresponds to a new [product_name] with firmware [version_no]. You need the matching software version. Please respond to my earlier questions.
Installed and started the software as an administrator, but nothing works.
Is your firewall or antivirus software active?

Hello, The device finally connected, but it took 10 minutes for the initial connection, then subsequent connections take only 5 seconds. Both my company and personal laptops behave the same way. Not sure why it happens, but I'll continue working like this for now. Thanks for your help.
I can't understand why this happens.

Hi, If your PC's IP is xxx.168.xxx.xxx and the device’s IP is xxx.169.xxx.xxx, it's not properly configured. Try disconnecting your PC from all networks except the direct Ethernet connection to the device, then run the software as admin. Use the Up/Download function. If only one interface is available, press the test button. A green check mark means communication is ready. Hope this helps.
Hello all, the device still won't connect. All settings are correct. Notably, Java is consuming all memory and CPU, as shown in the attached picture. This happens on both of my computers.
Consider starting a support request.

Hello everyone, Support has yet to respond to my request. I still can't connect my PC with the [product_name] ([article_no])—firmware [version_no], using [product_name] version [version_no]. [product_name] address: 192.168.2.239 255.255.255.0 Gateway: 0.0.0.0 PC address: 192.168.2.238 255.255.255.0 Gateway: blank I'm connecting via USB Ethernet adapter. Do I need to adjust firewall or permissions on this company laptop? Ping works. Any suggestions?

It's difficult to help since your details keep changing. Sometimes you say you can connect, then you say you can't. You also change address settings or omit important details, and now you've mentioned using a USB Ethernet adapter for the first time. It's hard to assist without consistent information.
I recently bought a USB Ethernet adapter and a switch for testing. I’m also trying different IPs by using my WiFi connection's IP.

Again, you say you can't connect and continue changing settings or leave out details. The USB Ethernet adapter is a new detail. Inconsistency makes it difficult to help. Thank you for all your attention and effort.

Hi everyone, update on my device connection issue. Switching to Safe Mode with Directory Services Restore in Windows 7 resulted in quick, successful connections and the ability to transfer programs. I need to investigate what changes regarding permissions and firewall settings between Safe Mode and normal startup. If anyone has suggestions, please let me know. I'll share the solution if I find it.

A new question published by [user_name] was moved to a separate thread, subject: Try to set connection with 2 PLC [version_no]: S7Connection doesn't work and displays a message. Best regards, [user_name]
Thank you everyone for your patience and dedication in helping me. Goodbye.

Keep in mind that using utilities providing advanced system control, such as god mode in combination with Windows 10 and Java, can negatively affect connectivity, explaining long connection times. Also, swapping the Ethernet cable can help, as ping may work without reliable data transfer if the cable isn't stable. Electrical interference or grounding issues might also play a role.

Thank you [user_name] for your response. I’ve tried all kinds of Ethernet cables, crossover and straight-through, plus USB adapter and switches between the device and computer. A friend who knows about [product_name] checked and it worked normally on his computer. Interestingly, switching my Windows 7 system to Directory Services Restore Mode allows normal connection. For now, I connect by using that mode. I'm unsure if I can run the machine this way long-term, but for now, it's working. Thanks again for your support.

analysis.insight_summary: The user experienced persistent connectivity problems between [product_name] software and the [product_name] hardware, despite trying basic troubleshooting steps such as changing IP settings and using different cables/adapters. The device could be detected but connection attempts caused the software and computer to freeze, often without any error messages. The lack of clear feedback led to confusion and halted progress, with frequent changes in setup and environmental details further complicating diagnosis.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects a seamless and stable connection between [product_name] software and hardware, along with immediate and clear error messages and troubleshooting steps when issues arise.
